targets.descriptor: Exeris Community + ADR-052 Blackbird JSON-mapper customizer (same 0.10.1 app jar + customizer uber-jar on the launch classpath; Jackson-3 invokedynamic response-encode accessors)
targets.eligibility_note: Within-exeris serialization-accessor A/B only (paired exeris-community__exeris-blackbird). Same exeris-community-app jar (kernel 0.10.1); the exeris-community-blackbird-customizer uber-jar is added to the launch classpath (ADR-052 ServiceLoader seam). Isolates Blackbird invokedynamic accessors vs the default megamorphic MethodHandle on the response-encode path. NOT a cross-runtime target; report only as a within-exeris tuning delta.

targets.descriptor: Serialisation-matrix arm 1: exeris-community-app pinned to kernel 0.10.1, default Jackson-3 MethodHandle accessors, pre-SegmentSink encode
targets.eligibility_note: WITHIN-EXERIS 2x2 serialisation matrix only (kernel version x Blackbird accessor). Built with -Dexeris.kernel.version=0.10.1 and launched from a version-staged jar so the arms cannot overwrite one another. Never report as a cross-runtime number.

targets.descriptor: Serialisation-matrix arm 2: kernel 0.10.1 + ADR-052 Blackbird customizer (invokedynamic accessors), pre-SegmentSink encode
targets.eligibility_note: WITHIN-EXERIS 2x2 serialisation matrix only. Same staged jar as exeris-k0101; the customizer uber-jar on the launch classpath is the ONLY difference. Leaf is valid only if the bootstrap breadcrumb '[exeris-blackbird] applied Jackson-3 BlackbirdModule' appears, proving the arm is not a silent no-op.

targets.descriptor: Serialisation-matrix arm 3: exeris-community-app pinned to kernel 0.10.2 (encode/allocation batch), default Jackson-3 MethodHandle accessors
targets.eligibility_note: WITHIN-EXERIS 2x2 serialisation matrix only. Differs from exeris-k0101 by the WHOLE v0.10.1..v0.10.2 range, not by SegmentSink alone: #241 response streaming plus #244 buffer-release accounting (#242 request-body streaming is inert for GET workloads). Label the contrast '0.10.2 encode/allocation batch', never 'SegmentSink'.

targets.descriptor: Serialisation-matrix arm 4: kernel 0.10.2 encode/allocation batch + ADR-052 Blackbird customizer
targets.eligibility_note: WITHIN-EXERIS 2x2 serialisation matrix only. The arm where an accessor/encode interaction would show: removing encode allocation raises the relative share of accessor cost, so Blackbird may pay more here than on 0.10.1. Same customizer jar as exeris-k0101-bb (seam byte-identical across the two kernel versions). Requires the same bootstrap-breadcrumb assertion.

targets.descriptor: Spring Boot + Hibernate ORM (JVM, virtual threads)

targets.descriptor: Spring Boot + Tomcat + Hibernate, servlet SecurityFilterChain DISABLED (same jar as spring-hibernate)
targets.default_protocol_note: protocol_mode is the fair-baseline default (community H1 loopback). H2C is reached via the run-guided protocol override (the legacy spring-app-axon saga label was the same jar/env at h2c). Persistence layer = Hibernate ORM.
targets.eligibility_note: Same module, same jar and same artifact_sha256 as spring-hibernate; the arms are separated by launch properties only (benchmark.security.filter-chain.enabled=false plus the three security auto-configuration exclusions). Exists solely to bound the security confound in the hosting rung of CLAIMS L3: spring-hibernate runs a per-request authorization decision that spring-on-exeris-pure does not, and that has never been measured on the Tomcat side. NOT a stack anyone would ship and not a comparator for anything else — pair it with spring-hibernate and nothing more.

targets.descriptor: Spring Boot + Tomcat, plain JDBC (JdbcTemplate, no ORM)
targets.default_protocol_note: protocol_mode is the fair-baseline default (community H1 loopback). ORM-free counterpart of spring-hibernate: same web layer (Tomcat + Spring MVC), Hibernate removed, hand-written SQL matching pure-native's shapes via JdbcTemplate. Isolates the ORM axis from the Exeris axis (see docs/CLAIMS.md L3 Amdahl ceiling).

targets.descriptor: Spring on Exeris (compatibility mode + Exeris Flow)
targets.eligibility_note: Baseline-candidate for request-path endpoints only. The compat request-scope bug was resolved by exeris-spring-runtime-web #48 (request-path DB access serves 2xx; verified in results/raw/guided/20260610T160359Z). Saga terminal-state metrics are NOT eligible: flow steps run on kernel worker VTs outside the request-scoped compat provider binding, so the saga never resolves (saga_success_rate=0, threshold_failure). This target is excluded from scenarios/e2e-shop-order-saga/comparative-pair-manifest.json and flagged baseline-only in tools/verify-target-asset-matrix.sh. See targets/exeris-spring-runtime-app-comp/README.md section 'Runtime eligibility'.

targets.descriptor: Spring on Exeris (pure mode, native ExerisRequestHandler)
targets.eligibility_note: mode=pure here means the Exeris side of the Pure-vs-Compat axis (no ExerisCompatDispatcher), which is NOT the same sense as spring-hibernate's mode=pure (plain Spring MVC on Tomcat, never routed through Exeris at all); both sit on the pure side of the axis but only this one is hosted by Exeris. Eligible for the full contract family, heavy and light, since exeris-spring-runtime #50 strips the query string before the pure-mode route lookup; the earlier heavy-only restriction is lifted. BUILD REQUIREMENT: light eligibility is a property of the runtime build, not of this target's source — a jar built against a pre-#50 runtime 404s on /api/v1/user?id=N while still passing every heavy contract, so check the runtime version before trusting a light result here. Verified 2026-08-02 on runtime-web 0.5.0-SNAPSHOT with kernel 0.10.2. BUILD PARITY: spring-on-exeris and spring-on-exeris-pure must be rebuilt together — they are matched at kernel 0.10.2 (raised from 0.9.0 by #50), and rebuilding one alone puts a kernel-version variable inside the compat-seam measurement. FOOTPRINT: RSS IS comparable with spring-on-exeris, correcting an earlier note here. Both arms boot the kernel SubsystemOrchestrator with Selector=ALL and start all eight subsystems including events and flow, so the missing exeris-spring-runtime-flow dependency removes Spring beans, not subsystems. Measured locally (n=1, two forced full GCs, identical flags and read-only load): 551 fewer classes and 2.59 MB less metaspace here, post-GC RSS 485 MB vs 483 MB on the compat arm — marginally higher, i.e. below noise and opposite in direction to the retired caveat. See targets/exeris-spring-runtime-app-pure/README.md. PUBLISHABLE — the former 'internal-only' stamp on this arm was withdrawn on 2026-08-11. It came from a CLAUDE.md line naming a path that never existed in this repo, added incidentally in an unrelated PR with no rationale on record; Exeris Spring Runtime is a product repo and has never been confidential. Pure-vs-Compat remains a mandatory LABELLING axis (never collapse a compat row into a pure one, route compat overhead to the compat/ track) — that is not a confidentiality boundary.

targets.descriptor: Spring on Exeris (pure mode, native ExerisRequestHandler + kernel-native persistence)
targets.eligibility_note: The only arm that is pure on BOTH axes. spring-on-exeris-pure is pure on the web axis only: it still runs Spring Data JPA + Hibernate over exeris-spring-runtime-data's ExerisDataSource (the compatibility DataSource), with exeris.runtime.data.compat-datasource.enabled=true. This target drops that module entirely — no JPA, no Hibernate, no Spring DataSource, no JdbcTemplate — and its repositories call eu.exeris.kernel.spi.persistence.TransactionalExecutor directly, executed by kernel-core TransactionOrchestrator over a per-request-scoped PersistenceEngine adapter (see ExerisPersistenceConfiguration). PRIMARY PAIR: spring-on-exeris-pure__spring-on-exeris-pure-native isolates the persistence axis — same web layer, same runtime, same kernel line, same pool config, same SQL result shapes. Against spring-hibernate or spring-on-exeris BOTH axes move at once; label such a leaf accordingly and do not attribute the delta to persistence alone. SQL PROVENANCE: every statement is copied verbatim from targets/exeris-community-app's UserRepository, so this arm and exeris-community issue byte-identical SQL. Change one, change both, or a runtime comparison silently becomes a query-plan comparison. TX BOUNDARY: no @Transactional on UserService — the read boundary is TransactionalExecutor's own (inReadSession for heavy, query for light). Layering Spring's transaction manager on top would acquire a second connection per request. This differs from the ORM arm by necessity and is part of what 'native persistence' means on this axis. "NATIVE" SCOPE: native repository API, NOT a native wire protocol. Community persistence is JDBC+HikariCP; the off-heap PgWire engine is Enterprise-only, so pgjdbc and Hikari are still on this classpath and in the measured path. Never label a run here 'Exeris native persistence' without that qualifier. BUILD PARITY: kernel is pinned INLINE on the dependencies (0.10.2), not via the kernel BOM — exeris-spring-runtime-bom inherits a dependencyManagement section from its parent that pins exeris-kernel-* to a newer line and wins over a later BOM import. Verify with `unzip -l <jar> | grep exeris-kernel` against the sibling arms after every build. The other three arms carry NO kernel pin and will drift to whatever the runtime BOM's parent resolves on their next rebuild. STATUS: built and jar-verified 2026-08-05; NOT yet boot-verified against a database. Run the Stage-4 preflight (/health, /db/ping, /api/v1/users) before using any leaf from this target. PUBLISHABLE — the former 'internal-only' stamp on this arm was withdrawn on 2026-08-11. It came from a CLAUDE.md line naming a path that never existed in this repo, added incidentally in an unrelated PR with no rationale on record; Exeris Spring Runtime is a product repo and has never been confidential. Pure-vs-Compat remains a mandatory LABELLING axis (never collapse a compat row into a pure one, route compat overhead to the compat/ track) — that is not a confidentiality boundary.

targets.descriptor: Spring on Exeris (compat mode, @RestController via ExerisCompatDispatcher + kernel-native persistence)
targets.eligibility_note: BLOCKED FOR CAMPAIGN USE AS OF 2026-08-08 — light contract only, and not for a reason in this repo. Against the latest PUBLISHED runtime snapshot (exeris-spring-runtime-web 0.5.0-20260805.182020-29) GET /api/v1/user?id=1 returns nothing (curl HTTP 000) because the compat ResponseEntity return-value handler throws IncompatibleClassChangeError: Spring Framework 7 removed MultiValueMap from HttpHeaders' interfaces (javap-verified against spring-web-7.0.8), and ExerisResponseEntityReturnValueHandler:65 calls HttpHeaders.putAll as a Map. Any @RestController returning ResponseEntity<T> dies in compat mode under Boot 4; heavy survives only because it returns List<UserView> and never enters that handler. A newer, UNPUBLISHED local build serves it — the fix exists but cannot be resolved from coordinates, so the arm waits for a published snapshot rather than being run on an irreproducible jar. Heavy is unaffected and was reproduced on the perf box. Fills the previously unmeasured cell of the two-axis grid: compat WEB layer over NATIVE persistence. The other three Exeris arms cover compat/ORM (spring-on-exeris), pure/ORM (spring-on-exeris-pure) and pure/native (spring-on-exeris-pure-native). AXES ARE NOT COUPLED — the finding this target was built for, and it survives the blocker: TransactionalExecutor resolves correctly under ExerisCompatDispatcher and the heavy contract returns 200 with a body byte-identical to all four ladder arms (heavy sha256/16 82f9bcdf2852bd5e), reproduced on the perf box 2026-08-08 against the published runtime. The light checksum 615734f3df404338 was obtained 2026-08-07 against the unpublished local build only. That was the open question this target was built to answer: KernelProviders.PERSISTENCE_ENGINE is a per-request ScopedValue whose coverage has NOT been universal in compat mode (the compat security filter ran outside it until runtime PR #48; flow-worker virtual threads still do). PRIMARY PAIR: spring-on-exeris-pure-native__spring-on-exeris-comp-native. Both targets build from the same POM — the two jars' BOOT-INF/lib listings diff empty — and differ by exactly one property, exeris.runtime.web.mode=compatibility. It is the only single-variable measurement of the Pure-vs-Compat WEB axis in this repo. Strict gate G3 classifies it non_eligible (mode pure vs compat) BY DESIGN: it is a compat-family overhead measurement, stored and labelled separately per the Pure-vs-Compat separation axis, not a cross-target comparative claim. DO NOT pair against spring-on-exeris expecting a persistence reading. That pair PASSES G3 (both mode=compat) and is the more confounded of the two: spring-on-exeris is still on Spring Boot 3.5.14 and Jackson 2 (com.fasterxml), outside the 2026-08-06 alignment, and additionally carries Spring Security and the flow stack. Gate eligibility is not fairness. SERIALISATION: nothing here encodes explicitly. ExerisCompatAutoConfiguration contributes exerisCompatJacksonConverter and ExerisCompatJsonConverterFactory selects JacksonJsonHttpMessageConverter off tools.jackson.databind on the classpath. That factory builds its own mapper, so pure-native's explicit JsonConfiguration/JsonEncoder pair has no counterpart here — same Jackson 3 defaults, different objects. Confirmed equal by body checksum, not assumed. "NATIVE" SCOPE: native repository API, NOT a native wire protocol — Community persistence is JDBC+HikariCP, so pgjdbc and Hikari remain in the measured path. Same qualifier as pure-native. BUILD PARITY: kernel pinned INLINE at 0.10.2, Boot 4.1.0, Jackson 3.1.4 — verified in the built jar, not inferred from the POM. Rebuild together with spring-on-exeris-pure-native, always. PUBLISHABLE — the former 'internal-only' stamp on this arm was withdrawn on 2026-08-11. It came from a CLAUDE.md line naming a path that never existed in this repo, added incidentally in an unrelated PR with no rationale on record; Exeris Spring Runtime is a product repo and has never been confidential. Pure-vs-Compat remains a mandatory LABELLING axis (never collapse a compat row into a pure one, route compat overhead to the compat/ track) — that is not a confidentiality boundary.

targets.default_protocol_note: protocol_mode is the fair-baseline default (community H1 loopback); health_url is cleartext h1 (fair baseline: same cleartext posture as exeris-community/spring-hibernate). H2C is reached via the run-guided protocol override (the legacy quarkus-app-axon saga label was the same jar/env at h2c). Persistence layer = Hibernate ORM.

targets.descriptor: Quarkus + pure JDBC, no ORM, tuned transport: native epoll + native BoringSSL TLS (JVM, virtual threads)
targets.eligibility_note: Tuned-transport (Netty native epoll + native BoringSSL TLS) pure-JDBC Quarkus; contrast with quarkus-hibernate which runs default Quarkus (JDK NIO + JSSE). Pure-JDBC also isolates Hibernate ORM cost (same SQL shapes, no ORM mapping layer). WIRED AND ELIGIBLE as of 2026-08-07 in scenarios/entity-read-by-id/comparative-pair-manifest.json for three pairs: quarkus-hibernate__quarkus-tuned (ORM cost within Quarkus), exeris-community__quarkus-tuned (runtime+transport, both no-ORM), and quarkus-tuned__spring-on-exeris-pure-native (cross-stack with ORM removed on both sides). The earlier 'not yet wired / justified-unused' text is retired. SERIALISATION FENCE: this target encodes with Jackson 2 (com.fasterxml) while every Exeris arm is on Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) since 2026-08-06. Profiling attributed roughly a fifth of Exeris on-CPU time in this scenario to Jackson 3's MethodHandle path, so any Exeris-vs-Quarkus row here carries a serialiser difference that works against Exeris and cannot be normalised away — each framework ships its own line. State it, and report cpu/req beside throughput. TRANSPORT LABELLING: 'tuned' is Netty native epoll, and the Exeris counterpart under mode=auto is posix-hybrid (NIO epoll + FFM syscalls), NOT io_uring. Verify the carrier from the target-app.log banner before labelling a run.

targets.descriptor: Restate durable-execution saga (JVM SDK 2.9, virtual threads) + pure JDBC
targets.default_protocol_note: protocol_mode h1 is the fair-baseline declaration: the k6-facing facade (JDK com.sun.net.httpserver) speaks HTTP/1.1 only — an h1-vs-h2c protocol mismatch against the canonical saga contracts and therefore a strict-gate disqualifier, same class as spring-on-exeris. Deployment unit is this JVM (facade :9004 + Restate SDK endpoint :9084) plus an external restate-server (ingress :8080, admin :9070) started by the saga baseline as compose service benchmark-restate-server.
targets.eligibility_note: Saga-only target (e2e-shop-order-saga CONTRACT-v2; v2 request-response model — terminal outcome in the POST /api/v1/orders 200 body, status polling served but normally skipped by k6). Not yet referenced by any comparative-pair-manifest or scenario.json fixed_contract; wire both (plus tools/verify-target-asset-matrix.sh) before any comparative claim. Like the Axon stacks, part of the deployment unit (restate-server container exeris-e2e-saga-restate-server) runs outside the per-process resource sampler — whole-deployment footprint claims must attribute it separately (logs/restate-server-docker-stats.csv). Durability tier: restate-server 1.7 default is T2 fsync node-durable (RocksDB WAL fsync per commit batch); cross-tier comparisons forbidden per CONTRACT-v2 s8.
